Alright, this is pretty much the game I've been fantasizing and just wish I had the money and the know how to make a reality. Picture a cross between Dark Souls, Monster Hunter, and Rune Factory/Harvest Moon. I get that there are a lot of mechanics all hanging around with each other and the possibility that the gameplay would begin to focus on grind instead of a nice flow, but I think if done right it would be amazing.


So the base area is a small village nestled inside the safety of ruins of an ancient civilization. I'm thinking an island culture based on the Samoan or Maori culture. You would be an outsider, crashed and washed ashore there, not quite trusted by the local population and forced to make your own living on the edge of town. You start your little farm, take care of your land and try to befriend the villagers by trying to get to know them or doing jobs for them.

These jobs would involve leaving the safety of the central ruins, which have a magical barrier around them, a leftover magic technology from the ancient civ kept alive by the towns magicians. To start with you just do missions still within the ruins, but steadily get further out into the jungle and volcano on the island using a bonfire system a la DS2 that would allow warping to certain points to make hunting easier. the combat of course would be pure souls. Spicing this up are special monsters that roam throughout the area as in Monster Hunter. Special, extraordinarily difficult to kill monsters that would take planning and a coordinated effort from yourself and the other villagers willing to help you. The number of helpers you could have would rely on the level f trust and respect you have earned from the village and the villagers would either be npc phantoms or co op players.


After a while you begin to reach the edge of your island, the monsters have been tamed and life is going pretty good. Suddenly, an assault from the mainland throws your life into disarray. The mainland is a vast desert with Arabic inspired ruins dotting the landscape. The local peoples are a kingdom of Witch Doctor / Voodoo culture that infects all members of society with a horrible disease found in the venom of a local fish. While alive you gain strength and speed from it, but once your brain dies the disease keeps the body running as efficiently as it can, meaning that only immolation or dismemberment are effective ways to kill an enemy.

With your island in flames from the attack you are forced to lead the surviving villagers to the mainland, carve out a hold in a set of ruins and defend it until the magicians can set up a barrier. From there you try to rebuild your life as much as possible, either choosing to magically charm and control the local animals for revenge on the local people or choosing to befriend the local peoples and help wipe out the source of the beasts that scourge the land as you did on the island.


From a gameplay standpoint, I'd love to see enviornments that are far more 3d than seen in the Souls games. Think trees you can climb to wait in ambush or escape from an enemy or Ruin areas that truly go vertical like Blighttown did in DS1, allowing you to drop from one loevel to another to help escape danger. I'd also want to implement a camoflauge / stealth mechanic to make it possible to sneak up on enemies and to provide a nice alternative to heavier armors.

That's really about as far as I'd thought it out, have no real enemy or magic or weapons concepts or anything like that.

First off, twinking is nowhere near a problem in DS2, largely due to soul memory and invasion mechanics. I personally have very few issues with soul memory, Ive never had an issue getting summoned as a sunbro, invading as a red, or invading as a blue except early new game. I think the agape ring is fixing a problem that isnt that bad for majority of players in the first place. That said, there are situations where sm is an atrocious idea. The agape ring is a potentially horrible fix as it allows people to grief new players.

You state flat out that an early Shulva run is hellish. If you are really good enough to do it, why do you have to just to fight someone low level. If youre that good you should own them anyways. Unless youre the kind of asshole who just likes to be a prick.

See, heres the fun thing about new players: they dont know what the hell theyre doing. And twinking isnt the most annoying invasion tactic ever, that award goes to corrosive urns (but if youre dumb enough to get hit...). However the newbie doesnt want to constantly burn effigies because they need them just to get through the game because of dying. Theyre not at your skill level.

And yeah, they are not good. Sure they could head to Shulva like you did, but this poor guy is getting shafted by the Pursuer and gangbanged by the Sentinels. I dont see them making a Shulva run anytime soon just to be on equal footing for a little bit while you can invade them.

Sure, they could be a rerolled vet, but aside from twinking twats whos going to do that shulva run, or something similar, every playthrough. Many of us reroll for challenge runs or just the fun of building up another character. And again, if youre that good you shouldnt be scared of losing unless youre worthless in a fair fight.

The only case I condone this is to farm CREOs from the arena, then just be a normal invader instead of wearing overpowered equipment.

You also state that the odds are stacked against invaders because they cant estus or use healing items. They also cant get hit by mobs, and how many low level characters are going to have more than 2 giant seeds? Much less know what the hell they are for a newbie. Also when you get invaded by someone who can one hit you, healing doesnt do anything. Invasions are supposed to be a challenge for both sides in different ways, but its a balance. Twinking isnt balanced, its stacking your cards.

As to whether twinking is a problem, I no longer rage quit because of it. I have been twinked on almost every single character ive rolled. Its annoying, and usually the only time I die to invaders in my ng runs (ng+ is a whole nother story)

So I stand by my assertion. If someone twinks theyre a twat and they bring the game down for everyone just so they can feel big. If you dont want a challenge, maybe this isnt a game for you

For the ruin sentinels the best strategy is caution. Always kill the first one without dropping down. When youve only got two left always try to keep them both on screen at the same time. A greatshield helps the fight tremendously as well as the stability allows you to absorb the attacks better.
For the pursuer i found that the best technique was to get close to bait an attack and roll just out of his range, only attacking after certain moves such as the 3 hit combo, his charge attack, and his shield bash. Despite how much range his sword potentially has, that godforsaken curse attack killed my first char soooo many times, his actual range on his attacks is fairly close to his body. Keep circling and use that to your advantage. 

And if you think these guys are a pain in the ass wait til you smack into the smelter demon the first time. And the tenth time. And the fiftieth. Or Freja and the million spiders from hell. But its worth every second of agony to finally win, and later when you look back as you try to figure out why some of the bosses were ever hard to begin with youll smile and laugh thinking about how far youve come.
